cover.headline: KFC is growing again and the stock trades well below its own history; the Sapphire merger is upside we do not pay for
cover.lead: Devyani runs 2,255 restaurants: KFC and Pizza Hut for Yum! in north, east and central India, KFC in Thailand (with Temasek as a 49% partner), Nigeria and Nepal, plus Costa Coffee, Biryani By Kilo and Vaango. FY26 revenue was ₹5,611 cr (+13%), EBITDA (before rent) ₹855 cr, and the owners lost ₹38.6 cr. KFC same-store sales turned positive in Q4FY26 (+4.9%) and Q1FY27 (+3.3%), and Q1FY27 EBITDA after rent rose 38%. We forecast EBITDA of ₹{{F.ebitda.0|num}} / {{F.ebitda.1|num}} / {{F.ebitda.2|num}} cr for FY27-29E. The street values Devyani on **EV/EBITDA** (after rent, 25-27x Mar/Jun-28E). The house rule (its own forward EV/EBITDA median since listing, 30.2x, adjusted by the QSR peers' −27.0% move against their five-year medians) gives **22x Sep-28E EBITDA of ₹1,249 cr, less Temasek's share of Thailand (~14.6% of the value) = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with BUY.** That is ≈33.5x after-rent EBITDA on the street's basis. Cross-checks are far lower (DCF ₹82, P/E ₹81). Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}. The Sapphire merger (CCI and NCLT approvals pending on 30-Sep-2026) is not in the base.

arguments.h: KFC has turned, and KFC is the business
arguments.p: KFC India is 63% of India revenue. After 13 quarters of falling same-store sales, SSSG was +4.9% in Q4FY26 and +3.3% in Q1FY27, dine-in rose to 57% of sales and brand contribution reached 17%. Management guides 5-6% SSSG and 100-120 new KFC stores a year; it says KFC brand margins pass 20% at ₹105-110k of daily sales per store (₹98k now). We model KFC India revenue +12% / +14% / +13% (stores +110 / 115 / 120).

arguments.h: Operating leverage is visible after rent
arguments.p: Q1FY27 EBITDA after rent was ₹151 cr (9.6% of revenue, +1.5 points), the highest ever, despite LPG and wage inflation. On our numbers after-rent EBITDA rises from ₹450 cr in FY26 to ₹808 cr in FY29E. But profit stays thin (EPS ₹{{F.eps.0|n2}} / ₹{{F.eps.1|n2}} / ₹{{F.eps.2|n2}}): depreciation and lease interest absorb most of the EBITDA, so the P/E is meaningless.

arguments.h: Half of Thailand is not Devyani's
arguments.p: Thailand (₹1,692 cr of revenue, 30% of the group) is held through a company that is 49% owned by Camas, a Temasek affiliate; the effective minority is 52.45%. We deduct ~₹3,617 cr for it (₹29 a share). Brokers who value consolidated EBITDA without this overstate the equity.

arguments.h: Valuation: cheap against its own past, not against cash flows
arguments.p: At ₹130.29 the stock trades at 17.7x Sep-28E EBITDA (grossed up for minorities), against a 30.2x forward median since listing; QSR peers trade 27% below their own five-year medians. The street's median target is ₹160 (4 post-results notes, all Buy). The DCF (₹82) says cash flows do not yet support the price: the rating rests on the multiple.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): KFC SSSG after +3.3% in Q1, store openings against the 200-225 plan (only -1 net in Q1), Pizza Hut losses.
Sapphire merger: CCI approval, then the NCLT petition (the exchange letters of Jun-2026 allow six months to file), creditor and shareholder meetings; management targets completion by end-FY27.
Yum! development agreements for the merged company, Pizza Hut waivers and the 19 Hyderabad KFC stores to be bought from Yum!.
KFC global initiatives in India (Kwench beverages, sauces, boneless) and the BBK dine-in and Express formats.
Rupee and baht: International (33% of revenue) gains when the rupee weakens.

sections.title: India's largest Yum! franchisee: 2,255 restaurants, two-thirds of the money from KFC

blocks.p: India's largest Yum! Brands franchisee: runs KFC and Pizza Hut in its Indian territories (Sapphire Foods holds the south/west and Sri Lanka), KFC in Thailand (via a 51:49 holding company with Camas, a Temasek affiliate), KFC and Pizza Hut in Nigeria and Nepal; also Costa Coffee, New York Fries and Sanook Kitchen in India (franchisee brands), and its own brands Vaango (South Indian), Biryani By Kilo and Goila Butter Chicken (Sky Gate, bought 2025) and food courts. 2,255 stores at 30-Jun-2026 (India 1,855; Thailand 323; Nigeria 39; Nepal 38). Devyani does not own KFC or Pizza Hut: it pays Yum! a royalty and continuing fees (₹363 cr, 6.5% of FY26 revenue) for exclusive development rights in its territories, and Costa Coffee similarly. Its own brands (Vaango, Biryani By Kilo, Goila Butter Chicken) are 5% of revenue.

blocks.callout: **How it makes money:** a KFC store sells ~₹98,000 a day (₹3.2 cr a year). Food and packaging take ~31% (gross margin ~69%); staff, rent, utilities, aggregator commissions, marketing and Yum!'s royalty take most of the rest, leaving a "brand contribution" of ~17% at KFC (Q1FY27). Head-office costs then take ~4-5 points, leaving ~9.6% "operating EBITDA" after rent for the group. Pizza Hut's stores sell a third as much from a similar cost base and lose money. Everything therefore hinges on daily sales per store (ADS): management says KFC margins pass 20% at ₹105-110k.

sections.title: Indian QSR: a US$30 bn market growing ~9% a year, now fought out on delivery apps

blocks.p: The company's annual report puts India's food-services market at ~US$94 bn in 2026, growing to ~US$153 bn by 2031 (~10.3% a year), and quick-service restaurants (QSR) at ~US$30 bn growing to ~US$47 bn (~9.3% a year). Growth drivers are the usual ones: incomes, urbanisation, nuclear families, women in work, and delivery apps. Management points to biryani alone as a ₹30,000-40,000 cr market whose largest brand sells only ₹300-350 cr.

bullets: Delivery has moved from under 10% of KFC's sales before Covid to ~45% (Q1FY27 call): aggregators now take share from dine-in rather than adding to it, and their own cheap-meal formats compete on price.

Three Yum! franchisees in India before the merger: Devyani (north, east, central), Sapphire Foods (south, west, Sri Lanka) and Yum! itself (19 KFC stores in Hyderabad, which Devyani will buy). Pizza Hut has been run through a three-way structure (Devyani, Sapphire, Yum!) that management blames for slow decisions.
KFC SSSG was negative for about 13 quarters to Q3FY26; it turned positive in Q4FY26 (+4.9%) and Q1FY27 (+3.3%).

blocks.callout: **So what:** the market grows ~9-10% a year, so a franchisee adding ~10% more stores a year needs positive same-store sales just to keep its margins. The structural change since Covid is delivery: it now eats into dine-in rather than adding to it, aggregators run their own cheap meals, and new chicken and pizza chains enter cheaply. That is why Devyani is pushing customers back into the stores.

sections.title: India: KFC back to growth (+11.7% in Q1FY27), Pizza Hut still shrinking, own brands the new leg

blocks.p: India revenue rose from ₹3,318 cr in FY25 to ₹3,752 cr in FY26 (+13.1%) and ₹1,058 cr in Q1FY27 (+14.5%, ~8% without the Biryani By Kilo base effect). **KFC** (₹2,374 cr, 783 stores at Mar-2026) grew 9.0% in FY26 on 87 net new stores while same-store sales fell 0.8%; in Q1FY27 revenue rose 11.7% with SSSG +3.3%, daily sales per store flat at ₹98k, dine-in up to 57% of sales and gross margin up 2.3 points to 69.4% as discounts on delivery were cut. **Pizza Hut** (₹721 cr) fell 1.6% in FY26 and Q1FY27 (SSSG -2.2%), closed 13 stores in Q1 and lost ₹3.6 cr at brand level; management will push it only after the merger simplifies decisions with Yum! and Sapphire. **Own brands** (₹98 cr in Q1FY27) and **Costa** (SSSG +10.2%) are growing fastest.

blocks.p: International revenue rose from ₹1,634 cr (FY25) to ₹1,859 cr (FY26, +13.8%) and ₹523 cr in Q1FY27 (+20.7%). Thailand (₹1,692 cr in FY26, 323 KFC stores) is 91% of it; KFC Thailand's daily sales per store have stayed at THB 54-57k for two years, so growth is new stores (24 added in FY26 across Thailand and Nepal) and a weaker rupee. Nepal (38 stores) is small but profitable (₹7 cr of profit in FY26); Nigeria (39 stores) lost money and has negative net worth. Brand contribution rose to 18.2% in Q1FY27 (+1.5 points) and EBITDA after rent to 12.6%.

sections.title: Two EBITDAs: 16.1% before rent, 9.6% after rent in Q1FY27

blocks.p: Under Ind AS 116, store rent is not an operating expense: it becomes depreciation of a "right-of-use" asset plus interest on a lease liability. Devyani's reported EBITDA (16.1% in Q1FY27) therefore excludes rent; its "operating EBITDA" (9.6%) deducts it. In FY26 the gap was ₹404 cr (lease principal ₹180 cr + lease interest ₹223 cr), 7.2% of revenue. The street values Devyani on the after-rent number; we value reported EBITDA with leases as debt (same economics, consistent with the stock's own history and the peers' Screener multiples).

bullets: **Gross margin** 69.1% in Q1FY27 (+0.9 points): price increases at KFC and Pizza Hut, fewer delivery discounts; LPG and dairy costs rose.

**Brand contribution** (store profit after rent, staff, utilities, marketing, royalty) 14.2% consolidated in Q1FY27 (KFC 17.0%, Pizza Hut -1.9%, own brands 10.2%, Costa and others 15.1%, International 18.2%).
**Head office** ~4.6% of revenue (brand contribution 14.2% less operating EBITDA 9.6%), down ~0.4 points in a year.
**Royalty** to Yum! and other franchisors ~6.5% of revenue: a permanent cost the owner-operators (Jubilant's Hong's, Devyani's BBK) do not pay.

blocks.callout: **So what:** after rent, Devyani earns under 10 paise per rupee of sales and depreciation of owned fit-outs takes most of that. A one-point gain in after-rent margin is worth ~₹60 cr of EBITDA a year, which is why ADS (daily sales per store) is the number to watch.

sections.title: The Sapphire merger: 46% more shares for a business of ~55% of Devyani's size; pending on 30-Sep-2026, so not in our base

blocks.p: On 1-Jan-2026 the boards agreed to merge Sapphire Foods (KFC and Pizza Hut in south and west India and Sri Lanka; FY26 revenue ₹3,125 cr, EBITDA ₹474 cr, Screener) into Devyani at 177 Devyani shares for every 100 Sapphire shares: 56.9 cr new shares, 46% of Devyani's 123.3 cr. Yum! supports the deal (new development agreements; Devyani to run Pizza Hut fully, buy 19 Yum!-run KFC stores in Hyderabad and pay a one-time fee of ~₹320 cr). Management claims ₹210-225 cr a year of net synergies (~60% in year one, all within two years). The appointed date is 1-Apr-2026. The exchanges cleared the scheme on 12-Jun-2026; on 26-Aug-2026 the planned purchase of 18.5% of Sapphire by Arctic International (an RJ Corp company) was dropped, so Sapphire's promoter takes Devyani shares instead. **On 30-Sep-2026 CCI and NCLT approvals were still pending** (management: completion by end-FY27). The merged company would have 180.2 cr shares with the RJ Corp group at 41.99%.

blocks.callout: **Our read:** at the 30-Sep close Sapphire traded at 1.63 Devyani shares against the 1.77 swap ratio, a 8% discount for time and deal risk. Whether the deal adds value depends on two things the market cannot yet see: Sapphire's worth (its shares have traded at lower multiples than Devyani's) and delivery of the synergies, which are management's estimate. If Sapphire is worth its market price, the swap alone dilutes our standalone value and the synergies must make up the gap; at our multiple it adds value even without them. Per PLAYBOOK §1 and the BELRISE precedent we keep a deal that needed regulatory approvals on 30-Sep-2026 out of the base and show it here.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** Narrow at best. Devyani's advantage is contractual, not owned: exclusive Yum! development rights for KFC and Pizza Hut in its territories, renewable at Yum!'s discretion, for a royalty of ~6.5% of revenue. KFC's brand is strong and chicken is the fastest-growing QSR category, but the brand belongs to Yum!, new chicken chains and aggregator meals are easy to try, and Pizza Hut has lost share to Domino's for years. Scale (2,255 stores) gives procurement and site-selection benefits that the Sapphire merger would roughly double.

sections.title: Revenue nearly tripled in four years (Thailand, Biryani By Kilo, stores); profit did not: FY26 was a loss

blocks.p: Revenue went from ₹2,084 cr in FY22 to ₹5,611 cr in FY26 (28% a year), but about ₹1,690 cr of FY26 revenue is Thailand (bought in January 2024) and own brands added ~₹230 cr, mostly Biryani By Kilo (bought in June 2025). India grew from ~₹3,318 cr (FY25) to ₹3,752 cr (FY26), +13%. EBITDA after Ind AS 116 (i.e. before rent) rose from ₹476 cr to ₹855 cr (company basis), but the margin fell from 22.8% (FY22, the post-Covid delivery boom) to 15.2%, as KFC same-store sales fell for 13 quarters, Pizza Hut shrank and Thailand came in at lower margins. After rent ("operating EBITDA") the margin went from 14.4% to 8.0%. Depreciation of stores and right-of-use assets (₹670 cr) and lease interest (₹223 cr) take almost all of it: net profit after minorities was ₹265 cr in FY23, ₹9 cr in FY25 and a loss of ₹38.6 cr in FY26.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** Devyani has bought growth (Thailand, BBK) faster than it has earned it. The Indian KFC engine stalled in FY24-FY26 (same-store sales down for 13 quarters) while the store count kept rising, so fixed costs grew faster than sales. The turn in KFC SSSG since Q4FY26 (+4.9%, +3.3%) is the first evidence of operating leverage in three years; EPS only becomes meaningful if that lasts.

**Sapphire merger completion by end-FY27; net synergies ₹210-225 cr a year at steady state (~2.5% of combined EBITDA base), ~60% in year one, 100% within two years; one-time fee to Yum! ~₹320 cr (to be capitalised)** (q1call; mergerPpt; mergerCall).
**Tech-related changes within existing budgets; no change in capex per store from the dine-in push** (q4call; q1call).

blocks.callout: **What we take from it:** the best quarter in two years, and the improvement is broad (KFC, own brands, Costa, International). The weak spots are store openings (−1 net in Q1 against 200-225 for the year: the new business-development team reset the pipeline) and Pizza Hut. Management called demand "stable" but warned about a below-normal monsoon, El Niño, LPG and the rupee.

blocks.p: Over FY22-26 Devyani generated ₹3,681 cr of operating cash and spent ₹2,171 cr on capex (Screener), plus ~₹1,090 cr (via the Temasek-co-owned holding company) for Thailand in FY24 and ₹420 cr in shares for Sky Gate in FY26. Operating cash is flattered by Ind AS 116: rent is paid in the financing section. In FY26 ₹919 cr of operating cash paid for ₹459 cr of capex (217 net new stores), ₹404 cr of lease payments (principal ₹180 cr, interest ₹223 cr) and ₹52 cr of other interest, leaving ₹4 cr. Devyani has never paid a dividend. Return on capital is low: Screener ROCE (incl. right-of-use assets and goodwill) ~5-6% since FY24.

sections.title: Clean audit; four things to adjust for: rent outside EBITDA, minorities, impairments and large intangibles

bullets: **EBITDA excludes rent.** Ind AS 116 moves ~₹404 cr of FY26 rent into depreciation and interest; operating cash flow (₹919 cr) therefore overstates cash earnings. We treat lease principal as capex in the forecasts and show EBITDA after rent.

**Minorities.** Camas (Temasek) owns 49% of the Thai holding company; FY26 profit attributable to minorities was −₹3.9 cr and +₹2.5 cr in Q1FY27. Screener's Net Profit row is before minorities; we use profit after minorities (DEVYANI.patch.js) and add ~7-21 points to the forecast tax rate for their share.

**Exceptional items and impairments.** FY26 had a ₹21.5 cr exceptional charge (Labour Code gratuity and leave, ₹12.2 cr, and other items) and ₹15.8 cr of store impairments; FY24 had a ₹151 cr post-tax exceptional gain (Screener). Impairments recur with store closures; we keep ~₹15 cr a year inside other income.

**Intangibles of ₹1,722 cr** (goodwill ₹683 cr, BBK brand ₹495 cr, Thai territory rights ₹413 cr, franchise rights ₹130 cr) exceed owners' equity; the auditors' key audit matter is their impairment test. The Thai unit showed an impairment indicator (performance below the acquisition case); no impairment was booked.
**Deferred tax.** FY26 had a ₹23 cr deferred tax credit on losses; future profits will be taxed at ~25% from the first rupee only after these are used.

**Options.** The Camas put is on the RJ Corp holding company and Devyani's call option on Camas's stake is not booked; if Devyani ever buys Camas out, it will be for cash at a price set in the agreement.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Joint auditors (Walker Chandiok, O P Bagla) gave an unmodified opinion and we found nothing improper. The amber reflects reported EBITDA that excludes the largest store cost, profit near zero after depreciation, and acquisition intangibles larger than equity that rest on management's projections.

sections.title: Net debt ₹3,336 cr at Mar-2026, of which ₹2,473 cr is store leases; ₹1,722 cr of goodwill and brands

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 Devyani had ₹1,361 cr of bank borrowings (long-term ₹786 cr, short-term ₹575 cr, incl. a ~₹240 cr bridge loan for the Thai equity infusion that management says was repaid in April 2026) and ₹2,473 cr of lease liabilities, against ₹497 cr of cash and investments. Screener counts leases as borrowings, so its net debt (₹3,336 cr) is the lease-inclusive figure; bank net debt was ~₹864 cr, about 1.9x FY26 EBITDA after rent (₹450 cr). Goodwill (₹683 cr), brands (₹495 cr, mostly BBK), territory rights (₹413 cr, Thailand) and franchise rights (₹130 cr) add up to ₹1,722 cr, more than the owners' equity of ₹1,542 cr. Minorities (mainly Camas in Thailand) hold another ₹343 cr of book equity. Working capital is negative: suppliers fund inventory.

blocks.p: The street uses EV/EBITDA on EBITDA after rent ("pre-Ind AS 116"), about 1.5-2 years forward (Mar-28E to Jun-28E), at 25-27x; one house uses a DCF. Because ~14.6% of the group's EBITDA belongs to Camas (Temasek) through Thailand, we value the parts at the group multiple and deduct the minorities' share. blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** the largest Yum! franchisee in India, with exclusive KFC and Pizza Hut rights in its territories, 2,255 restaurants, a KFC business that has just returned to same-store growth (+3.3% in Q1FY27) and record after-rent EBITDA (9.6% margin), half of a growing KFC Thailand, and an option on the Sapphire merger. You are also buying a Pizza Hut business that loses money, thin profits after depreciation and rent, ~₹1,722 cr of acquisition intangibles and a promoter structure that has paid for deals in shares.

**What you are paying:** ₹130.29 is 17.7x Sep-28E EBITDA (minorities grossed up) and ≈25.7x after-rent EBITDA on the street's basis, against a 30.2x forward median since listing; QSR peers are 27% below their five-year medians. On earnings (174.5x FY28E EPS) and on cash flows (DCF ₹82 before minorities) the stock is not cheap. The rule gives BUY because the multiple, not the cash, is low.

**This is a multiple call more than an earnings call.** Our EBITDA is ~5% below the street for FY28E; our target is above the street's ₹160 median because Devyani's own five-year history (median 30.2x forward) is richer than the 25-27x after-rent multiples brokers now use, and the sector move (-27.0%) does not take all of that away.
**Biggest swing factors:** the multiple (each 1x of Sep-28E EBITDA is ~₹9 a share after minorities) and the margin (each point of Sep-28E EBITDA margin moves the target by ~₹11).

The accounting rule for leases: store rent is booked as depreciation of a right-of-use asset plus interest on a lease liability, not as an operating cost.
Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation as reported; under Ind AS 116 it excludes rent.
EBITDA after deducting rent; the measure the street's multiples use.
Store-level profit of a brand after food, staff, rent, utilities, marketing and royalty, before head-office costs.
Same-store sales growth: revenue growth of stores open at least a year.
Outside shareholders in a subsidiary; here mainly Camas (Temasek), with 49% of the company that owns KFC Thailand.
Sum of the parts: each part valued separately, then debt and minorities deducted.

Half of FY28E plus half of FY29E: the 12-month-forward earnings the market will look at in September 2027.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Devyani International (consolidated, Rs crore), standalone: the Sapphire Foods merger was still awaiting CCI and NCLT approval on 30-Sep-2026, so it is not in the base (pro-forma shown as a sensitivity, BELRISE precedent). FY26 (Mar-2026) is the base year. Two parts: India (KFC, Pizza Hut, Costa and other franchisee brands, Vaango, Biryani By Kilo, food courts) and International (KFC Thailand, KFC/Pizza Hut Nigeria and Nepal), each with revenue growth and EBITDA margin after Ind AS 116 (rent excluded). India revenue is built from KFC stores x revenue per store plus the other brands (businessLines), checked in DEVYANI.ctx.js. Minorities (52.45% effective of Thailand via Camas/Temasek; 12.69% of Nigeria) sit in the tax line for EPS and are deducted in the SOTP.

segments.name: India
segments._why: India revenue +13.1% in FY26 (Rs3,318 cr to Rs3,752 cr; KFC +9.0% on 87 net new stores with SSSG -0.8%, Pizza Hut -1.6%, own brands +Rs231 cr from Biryani By Kilo, bought 10-Jun-2025); Q1FY27 +14.5% (KFC +11.7%, SSSG +3.3%; Pizza Hut -1.6%; own brands +Rs63 cr, mostly the BBK base effect, so +7-8% excluding it). Built from KFC stores (100-120 net adds guided for FY27; we assume 110 / 115 / 120) x revenue per average store (-1.0% / +0.5% / +1.0%: SSSG 3-5% less new-store dilution) plus Pizza Hut (no net new stores in calendar 2026; -1.5% / +3% / +5%), own brands (+32% / +20% / +18%), Costa and other franchisee brands (+7% / +10% / +10%) and food courts and other (+5%).
segments._marginWhy: India EBITDA margin (post-Ind AS) 18.8% in FY25, 16.1% in FY26 (KFC SSSG negative for 13 quarters to Q3FY26, Pizza Hut losses at brand level, BBK consolidation). India operating EBITDA (pre-Ind AS) 8.0% in Q1FY27 vs 7.1% a year earlier; KFC brand contribution 17.0% (+1.4 points). We assume 16.6% / 17.2% / 17.8%: KFC ADS creeping towards the Rs105-110k at which management says brand margin passes 20%, offset by Pizza Hut (brand contribution still negative) and LPG and wage inflation. No merger synergies (merger not approved by 30-Sep-2026).

segments.name: International
segments.marginLabel: EBITDA (after Ind AS 116; consolidated less India)
segments._why: International revenue +13.8% in FY26 (Thailand Rs1,692 cr, +13.7%; Nigeria and Nepal Rs168 cr); Q1FY27 +20.7% (Rs523 cr), helped by a weaker rupee (Rs95.6 to the US dollar in July 2026) and 24 new stores in the year. Thailand KFC ADS has been flat at THB 55-57k for two years, so growth is mostly stores and currency. We assume +17% / +12% / +11% with ~20-25 net new stores a year and no further rupee depreciation after FY27.
segments._marginWhy: International EBITDA margin (post-Ind AS) 13.3% (FY25), 13.5% (FY26); brand contribution 17.1% (FY26) and 18.2% in Q1FY27 (+1.5 points); operating EBITDA (pre-Ind AS) 12.6% in Q1FY27 vs 10.2% a year earlier. We assume 14.5% / 14.8% / 15.0%.

assumptions._unallocWhy: International EBITDA is consolidated less India, so the two parts add to the company's EBITDA by construction.
assumptions._esopWhy: Share-based payment (Rs2.4 cr in FY26, AR cash flow) is inside segment EBITDA; the array is kept at zero for the Excel model.

businessLines._why: India revenue = KFC (average stores x revenue per average store) + Pizza Hut + own brands + franchisee brands + food courts and other. FY26: KFC Rs2,373.7 cr on 739.5 average stores (696 to 783) = Rs3.210 cr per store; Pizza Hut Rs720.6 cr; own brands Rs305.9 cr; franchisee brands Rs213.3 cr; other Rs138.6 cr (India revenue less the four brand groups; includes food courts and the inter-company elimination).

assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex plus lease principal, because reported EBITDA excludes rent (JUBLFOOD/LENSKART treatment). Cash capex (PPE and intangibles) Rs491 cr (FY25), Rs459 cr (FY26) for 217 net new stores; 200-225 net new stores guided for FY27 at an unchanged capex per store. We assume Rs480 / 520 / 560 cr. Lease principal Rs141.5 cr (FY25), Rs180.4 cr (FY26); we assume Rs200 / 225 / 250 cr.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation and impairment Rs670 cr (Screener) = 8.3% of average gross block (Rs8,044 cr incl. right-of-use assets). Q1FY27 depreciation Rs180.4 cr plus impairment Rs1.1 cr (~Rs726 cr annualised). 7.75% gives FY27E ~Rs722 cr; the engine never retires assets, so a rate a little below history keeps depreciation near 11% of revenue (11.9% in FY26).
assumptions._treasuryWhy: The model's net treasury is negative (borrowings Rs1,361 cr and lease liabilities Rs2,473 cr against Rs497 cr of cash and investments at Mar-2026), so no yield is applied; interest on deposits is in the fixed other income.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Company other income Rs37.0 cr (FY25) and Rs45.1 cr (FY26: interest Rs15.7 cr, gains on lease terminations Rs23.8 cr, write-backs and other); Screener's line nets impairment, exchange differences and exceptional items against it (FY26 Rs31 cr; trailing four quarters to Jun-2026 Rs30 cr). Q1FY27 company other income Rs19.2 cr. We assume Rs50 / 55 / 60 cr net of ~Rs15 cr a year of store impairments: above the trailing figure (which carries the Rs21.5 cr exceptional Labour Code charge) and below the Q1 run-rate.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs275.7 cr = lease interest Rs223.4 cr + interest on borrowings ~Rs52 cr; Q1FY27 Rs70.1 cr (Rs280 cr annualised). Lease interest grows ~8% a year with the store base (Rs240 / 258 / 278 cr); bank interest edges down (Rs45 / 42 / 40 cr) as the short-term loan raised for the Thai equity infusion was repaid in April 2026 (management, Q4 call).
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax ~25% of PBT (Q1FY27 Rs5.8 cr on Rs22.9 cr). The engine has no minority line, so minorities' share of profit (Rs2.5 cr in Q1FY27; we assume ~Rs10 / 13 / 16 cr) is added to the tax rate: 25% + 21 / 9 / 7 points on our PBT of ~Rs47 / 139 / 240 cr.

capexBuild._why: Engine capex = cash capex + lease principal (checked in DEVYANI.ctx.js).

rentBuild._why: Rent under Ind AS 116 = lease principal + lease interest (cash), used to translate our post-Ind AS EBITDA into the pre-Ind AS (after-rent) 'operating EBITDA' the street values. FY26: principal Rs180.4 cr + interest Rs223.4 cr = Rs403.8 cr, equal to reported less operating EBITDA (Rs855.4 cr less Rs450.1 cr = Rs405.3 cr). FY25: Rs141.5 cr + Rs206.0 cr = Rs347.5 cr (Rs842.2 cr less Rs494.3 cr = Rs347.9 cr).

minorities._why: Devyani owns 51% of Devyani International DMCC, which holds the Thai KFC business (Restaurants Development Co.); Camas (a Temasek affiliate) owns 49%; through the Thai holding companies the effective non-controlling interest is 52.45% (AR FY26 note 51). Thailand is 91% of International revenue (Rs1,692 cr of Rs1,859 cr); we assume the same share of International EBITDA. Nigeria's minorities (12.69% at RV Enterprizes, 31.25% at the Nigerian company) hold a negative net worth and are ignored. Minorities' claim in the SOTP = 52.45% x Thailand's share of group EBITDA x equity value before minorities (assumes Thailand carries the group's leverage per rupee of EBITDA). Camas's put option is written on the RJ Corp holding company, not on Devyani; Devyani's call option is not booked (AR FY26 note 44).

dcf._betaWhy: Beta 0.85 gives 11.6%, which we use as the discount rate: a WACC of ~11.6% with lease liabilities and bank debt at ~17% of enterprise value (cost of equity ~12.5%, after-tax cost of debt and leases ~7.5%). The engine discounts at one rate, so beta is set to land on the WACC (PLAYBOOK §7).
dcf._tgWhy: Eating out is under-penetrated in India and KFC is the fastest-growing Yum! brand there; Thailand is mature. 5.5%, mid-range of the house 5-6%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~11-12% in FY29E to 8% by FY42E.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA (after Ind AS 116) edges from 16.9% (FY29E) to 18.5% (FY25 was 17.0%): operating leverage at KFC, partly absorbed by Pizza Hut and wage, rent and aggregator costs.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex incl. lease principal fades from ~10.2% of revenue (FY29E) to 9% (cash capex ~6%, lease principal ~3%); depreciation incl. right-of-use 9% long run (11.9% in FY26).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: KFC SSSG reaches the 5-6% guide from H2FY27 and ADS passes Rs105k by FY28, lifting KFC brand margin towards 20%; Pizza Hut turns brand-positive; BBK compounds; Thailand keeps adding stores with a stable baht.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: KFC SSSG slips back to zero as aggregators' cheap meals and new chicken chains take share; Pizza Hut keeps shrinking; LPG, wage and rent inflation keep India margins flat; Thai consumer weakness and a stronger rupee cut International growth.
